atlas.name: HCP-MMP1.0 (Glasser et al. 2016)
atlas.description: Multi-modal parcellation of the cerebral cortex into 180 areas per hemisphere, based on cortical thickness, myelin maps, resting-state and task fMRI from the Human Connectome Project.

reference.text: Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536, 171-178.

atlas.data_source: Vertex labels on fsLR 32k from micapipe (MICA-MNI); region abbreviations from the Glasser et al. 2016 supplementary table.
atlas.note: Only regions listed below have curated descriptions. All other regions show their atlas abbreviation only.

V1.location: Occipital lobe, banks of the calcarine sulcus (medial surface).
V1.function: First cortical stage of visual processing. Contains a retinotopic map of the contralateral visual hemifield; neurons are tuned to orientation, spatial frequency and ocular dominance.

references.text: Wandell BA, Dumoulin SO, Brewer AA (2007). Visual field maps in human cortex. Neuron 56, 366-383.

V2.location: Occipital lobe, surrounding V1 on the medial and lateral surface.
V2.function: Second retinotopic map; receives most of its input from V1 and processes contours, texture and binocular disparity.

references.text: Wandell BA, Dumoulin SO, Brewer AA (2007). Visual field maps in human cortex. Neuron 56, 366-383.

V4.location: Ventral occipital cortex, anterior to V3.
V4.function: Involved in colour and form processing; human V4 (hV4) is retinotopically organised. Its exact homology with macaque V4 is debated.

references.text: Zeki S et al. (1991). A direct demonstration of functional specialization in human visual cortex. J Neurosci 11, 641-649.
Wandell BA, Dumoulin SO, Brewer AA (2007). Visual field maps in human cortex. Neuron 56, 366-383.

MT.location: Lateral occipito-temporal cortex, near the ascending limb of the inferior temporal sulcus.
MT.function: Core of the human motion complex (MT+/V5): responds strongly to visual motion and is involved in perceiving motion direction and speed.

references.text: Zeki S et al. (1991). A direct demonstration of functional specialization in human visual cortex. J Neurosci 11, 641-649.
Tootell RB et al. (1995). Functional analysis of human MT and related visual cortical areas using magnetic resonance imaging. J Neurosci 15, 3215-3230.

FFC.location: Ventral temporal cortex, lateral fusiform gyrus.
FFC.function: Responds more strongly to faces than to other objects (fusiform face area). The Glasser parcel is larger than the classic fMRI-defined FFA and also covers neighbouring object-selective cortex.
FFC.status: established (parcel boundaries differ from the classic FFA)

references.text: Kanwisher N, McDermott J, Chun MM (1997). The fusiform face area: a module in human extrastriate cortex specialized for face perception. J Neurosci 17, 4302-4311.

A1.location: Heschl's gyrus (transverse temporal gyrus), inside the Sylvian fissure.
A1.function: Core auditory cortex with tonotopic organisation (orderly map of sound frequency).

references.text: Moerel M, De Martino F, Formisano E (2014). An anatomical and functional topography of human auditory cortical areas. Front Neurosci 8, 225.

4.location: Precentral gyrus and anterior bank of the central sulcus.
4.function: Origin of much of the corticospinal tract; somatotopically organised (motor homunculus) control of contralateral body movements.

references.text: Penfield W, Boldrey E (1937). Somatic motor and sensory representation in the cerebral cortex of man as studied by electrical stimulation. Brain 60, 389-443.

3b.location: Posterior bank of the central sulcus / postcentral gyrus.
3b.function: Primary somatosensory cortex in the strict sense: somatotopic representation of cutaneous touch from the contralateral body.

references.text: Kaas JH (1983). What, if anything, is SI? Organization of first somatosensory area of cortex. Physiol Rev 63, 206-231.
Penfield W, Boldrey E (1937). Somatic motor and sensory representation in the cerebral cortex of man as studied by electrical stimulation. Brain 60, 389-443.

44.location: Inferior frontal gyrus, pars opercularis (posterior part of Broca's region).
44.function: Part of Broca's region. Involved in speech production and syntactic processing; also engaged by non-linguistic tasks such as action observation and sequencing, so its role is not language-specific.

references.text: Amunts K et al. (1999). Broca's region revisited: cytoarchitecture and intersubject variability. J Comp Neurol 412, 319-341.
Hagoort P (2005). On Broca, brain, and binding: a new framework. Trends Cogn Sci 9, 416-423.

45.location: Inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (anterior part of Broca's region).
45.function: Part of Broca's region. Associated with semantic processing and controlled retrieval of word meaning; typically left-lateralised for language.

references.text: Amunts K et al. (1999). Broca's region revisited: cytoarchitecture and intersubject variability. J Comp Neurol 412, 319-341.
Hagoort P (2005). On Broca, brain, and binding: a new framework. Trends Cogn Sci 9, 416-423.

FEF.location: Precentral sulcus near its junction with the superior frontal sulcus.
FEF.function: Control of voluntary saccadic eye movements and shifts of visuospatial attention; node of the dorsal attention network.

references.text: Paus T (1996). Location and function of the human frontal eye-field: a selective review. Neuropsychologia 34, 475-483.
Corbetta M, Shulman GL (2002). Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain. Nat Rev Neurosci 3, 201-215.

55b.location: Precentral gyrus, between the frontal eye field and premotor cortex.
55b.function: Newly delineated in HCP-MMP1.0; activated by the HCP language task (story versus maths contrast). Its function is not yet well characterised beyond this.

references.text: Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536, 171-178.

PSL.location: Posterior end of the Sylvian fissure, at the temporo-parietal junction.
PSL.function: Named in HCP-MMP1.0 for its activation in the language task contrast. Lies near classic 'Wernicke's area' territory, but the parcel is defined multimodally, not clinically.

references.text: Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536, 171-178.

EC.location: Anterior medial temporal lobe, parahippocampal gyrus.
EC.function: Main interface between neocortex and hippocampus; involved in memory and spatial navigation (grid-cell-like signals reported in humans).

references.text: Doeller CF, Barry C, Burgess N (2010). Evidence for grid cells in a human memory network. Nature 463, 657-661.

V3.location: Occipital lobe, surrounding V2 dorsally and ventrally.
V3.function: Third retinotopic map of the contralateral hemifield; part of early visual cortex.

references.text: Wandell BA, Dumoulin SO, Brewer AA (2007). Visual field maps in human cortex. Neuron 56, 366-383.

MST.location: Lateral occipito-temporal cortex, anterior to MT; part of the MT+ complex.
MST.function: Motion processing with large receptive fields that include the ipsilateral visual field; implicated in optic-flow and self-motion analysis.

references.text: Huk AC, Dougherty RF, Heeger DJ (2002). Retinotopy and functional subdivision of human areas MT and MST. J Neurosci 22, 7195-7205.

LO1.location: Lateral occipital cortex, between V3d and MT.
LO1.function: Retinotopically organised part of the lateral occipital complex, which responds to objects and shapes.

references.text: Larsson J, Heeger DJ (2006). Two retinotopic visual areas in human lateral occipital cortex. J Neurosci 26, 13128-13142.
Grill-Spector K, Kourtzi Z, Kanwisher N (2001). The lateral occipital complex and its role in object recognition. Vision Res 41, 1409-1422.

LO2.location: Lateral occipital cortex, anterior to LO1.
LO2.function: Second retinotopic map in the lateral occipital complex; object and shape processing.

references.text: Larsson J, Heeger DJ (2006). Two retinotopic visual areas in human lateral occipital cortex. J Neurosci 26, 13128-13142.
Grill-Spector K, Kourtzi Z, Kanwisher N (2001). The lateral occipital complex and its role in object recognition. Vision Res 41, 1409-1422.

3a.location: Depth of the central sulcus, between motor area 4 and area 3b.
3a.function: Proprioceptive somatosensory cortex: receives muscle-spindle input about limb position.

references.text: Kaas JH (1983). What, if anything, is SI? Organization of first somatosensory area of cortex. Physiol Rev 63, 206-231.

1.location: Crown of the postcentral gyrus, posterior to 3b.
1.function: Somatosensory area processing cutaneous input, e.g. texture; contains its own somatotopic map.

references.text: Kaas JH (1983). What, if anything, is SI? Organization of first somatosensory area of cortex. Physiol Rev 63, 206-231.

2.location: Posterior postcentral gyrus, anterior bank of the postcentral sulcus.
2.function: Somatosensory area integrating proprioceptive and tactile input, e.g. for object shape and size.

references.text: Kaas JH (1983). What, if anything, is SI? Organization of first somatosensory area of cortex. Physiol Rev 63, 206-231.

6mp.location: Medial superior frontal gyrus, posterior part (supplementary motor area territory).
6mp.function: Corresponds roughly to the supplementary motor area (SMA): movement sequencing and initiation, bimanual coordination.

references.text: Nachev P, Kennard C, Husain M (2008). Functional role of the supplementary and pre-supplementary motor areas. Nat Rev Neurosci 9, 856-869.

6ma.location: Medial superior frontal gyrus, anterior to 6mp (pre-SMA territory).
6ma.function: Corresponds roughly to the pre-supplementary motor area: cognitive aspects of action such as switching, inhibition and sequence learning.

references.text: Nachev P, Kennard C, Husain M (2008). Functional role of the supplementary and pre-supplementary motor areas. Nat Rev Neurosci 9, 856-869.

SCEF.location: Medial frontal cortex, dorsal to the cingulate sulcus.
SCEF.function: Named for activation during eye-movement tasks in the HCP data; the supplementary eye field is known from monkey work, but the human parcel is less well characterised.

references.text: Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536, 171-178.

RSC.location: Medial parietal cortex, posterior to the splenium of the corpus callosum.
RSC.function: Scene processing and spatial navigation, especially orienting the viewer within a familiar environment and memory for places.

references.text: Epstein RA (2008). Parahippocampal and retrosplenial contributions to human spatial navigation. Trends Cogn Sci 12, 388-396.

PHA1.location: Medial ventral temporal lobe, parahippocampal gyrus.
PHA1.function: Part of the parahippocampal place area, which responds strongly to scenes and spatial layouts.

references.text: Epstein R, Kanwisher N (1998). A cortical representation of the local visual environment. Nature 392, 598-601.
Epstein RA (2008). Parahippocampal and retrosplenial contributions to human spatial navigation. Trends Cogn Sci 12, 388-396.

PHA2.location: Medial ventral temporal lobe, parahippocampal gyrus.
PHA2.function: Part of the parahippocampal place area, which responds strongly to scenes and spatial layouts.

references.text: Epstein R, Kanwisher N (1998). A cortical representation of the local visual environment. Nature 392, 598-601.
Epstein RA (2008). Parahippocampal and retrosplenial contributions to human spatial navigation. Trends Cogn Sci 12, 388-396.

PHA3.location: Medial ventral temporal lobe, parahippocampal gyrus.
PHA3.function: Part of the parahippocampal place area, which responds strongly to scenes and spatial layouts.

references.text: Epstein R, Kanwisher N (1998). A cortical representation of the local visual environment. Nature 392, 598-601.
Epstein RA (2008). Parahippocampal and retrosplenial contributions to human spatial navigation. Trends Cogn Sci 12, 388-396.

H.location: Medial temporal lobe; only the part reaching the cortical surface model is included in this parcel.
H.function: Essential for forming new declarative memories and for spatial memory; damage causes anterograde amnesia.

references.text: Scoville WB, Milner B (1957). Loss of recent memory after bilateral hippocampal lesions. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 20, 11-21.
Squire LR (1992). Memory and the hippocampus: a synthesis from findings with rats, monkeys, and humans. Psychol Rev 99, 195-231.

PeEc.location: Anterior medial temporal lobe, lateral to the entorhinal cortex.
PeEc.function: Object recognition memory and fine object discrimination at the interface of visual perception and memory.

references.text: Murray EA, Bussey TJ, Saksida LM (2007). Visual perception and memory: a new view of medial temporal lobe function in primates and rodents. Annu Rev Neurosci 30, 99-122.

AVI.function: Interoception and subjective feeling states; a core node of the salience network.

references.text: Craig AD (2009). How do you feel - now? The anterior insula and human awareness. Nat Rev Neurosci 10, 59-70.

AAIC.location: Anterior insula, agranular part near the frontal operculum.
AAIC.function: Interoception, emotional awareness and salience processing.

references.text: Craig AD (2009). How do you feel - now? The anterior insula and human awareness. Nat Rev Neurosci 10, 59-70.

a24pr.location: Dorsal anterior cingulate / anterior midcingulate cortex.
a24pr.function: Integrates negative affect, pain and cognitive control; involved in adaptive control of behaviour.

references.text: Shackman AJ et al. (2011). The integration of negative affect, pain and cognitive control in the cingulate cortex. Nat Rev Neurosci 12, 154-167.

p24pr.location: Dorsal midcingulate cortex, posterior to a24pr.
p24pr.function: Midcingulate region involved in cognitive control, pain and motor-related processing.

references.text: Shackman AJ et al. (2011). The integration of negative affect, pain and cognitive control in the cingulate cortex. Nat Rev Neurosci 12, 154-167.

v23ab.function: Core of the default mode network: internally directed cognition, memory retrieval and self-referential thought.

references.text: Leech R, Sharp DJ (2014). The role of the posterior cingulate cortex in cognition and disease. Brain 137, 12-32.

d23ab.function: Posterior cingulate region of the default mode network; its dorsal part also interacts with attention and control networks.

references.text: Leech R, Sharp DJ (2014). The role of the posterior cingulate cortex in cognition and disease. Brain 137, 12-32.

31pv.function: Part of the posterior cingulate hub of the default mode network.

references.text: Leech R, Sharp DJ (2014). The role of the posterior cingulate cortex in cognition and disease. Brain 137, 12-32.

PGi.function: Semantic processing, memory retrieval and social cognition; part of the default mode network.

references.text: Seghier ML (2013). The angular gyrus: multiple functions and multiple subdivisions. Neuroscientist 19, 43-61.

PGs.function: Angular gyrus subdivision involved in memory retrieval, semantic processing and attention to internal representations.

references.text: Seghier ML (2013). The angular gyrus: multiple functions and multiple subdivisions. Neuroscientist 19, 43-61.

TPOJ1.location: Posterior superior temporal sulcus / temporo-parietal junction.
TPOJ1.function: Lies in the temporo-parietal junction territory associated with theory of mind and social cognition; the correspondence between the parcel and functionally defined TPJ is approximate.

references.text: Saxe R, Kanwisher N (2003). People thinking about thinking people: the role of the temporo-parietal junction in 'theory of mind'. NeuroImage 19, 1835-1842.

STSdp.location: Posterior superior temporal sulcus, dorsal bank.
STSdp.function: Social perception: biological motion, faces in motion and voices; the superior temporal sulcus is functionally heterogeneous.

references.text: Hein G, Knight RT (2008). Superior temporal sulcus - it's my area: or is it? J Cogn Neurosci 20, 2125-2136.

LBelt.location: Lateral to A1 on Heschl's gyrus / superior temporal plane.
LBelt.function: Auditory belt cortex: second stage of cortical auditory processing with tonotopic organisation.

references.text: Moerel M, De Martino F, Formisano E (2014). An anatomical and functional topography of human auditory cortical areas. Front Neurosci 8, 225.

MBelt.location: Medial to A1 on the superior temporal plane.
MBelt.function: Auditory belt cortex surrounding the core; tonotopically organised.

references.text: Moerel M, De Martino F, Formisano E (2014). An anatomical and functional topography of human auditory cortical areas. Front Neurosci 8, 225.

PBelt.location: Lateral superior temporal gyrus, lateral to the belt areas.
PBelt.function: Auditory parabelt cortex: higher-order auditory processing beyond core and belt.

references.text: Moerel M, De Martino F, Formisano E (2014). An anatomical and functional topography of human auditory cortical areas. Front Neurosci 8, 225.

10pp.function: Anterior prefrontal cortex: integrating outcomes of multiple cognitive operations, e.g. during multitasking and prospective memory.

references.text: Ramnani N, Owen AM (2004). Anterior prefrontal cortex: insights into function from anatomy and neuroimaging. Nat Rev Neurosci 5, 184-194.

46.location: Middle frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
46.function: Working memory, especially monitoring and manipulation of information held in mind.

references.text: Petrides M (2005). Lateral prefrontal cortex: architectonic and functional organization. Phil Trans R Soc B 360, 781-795.

9-46d.location: Dorsal middle frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
9-46d.function: Executive functions and monitoring within working memory.

references.text: Petrides M (2005). Lateral prefrontal cortex: architectonic and functional organization. Phil Trans R Soc B 360, 781-795.

OFC.location: Orbital surface of the frontal lobe.
OFC.function: Representation of reward value and hedonic experience; guides decision making.

references.text: Kringelbach ML (2005). The human orbitofrontal cortex: linking reward to hedonic experience. Nat Rev Neurosci 6, 691-702.

13l.function: Orbitofrontal area involved in reward value and reinforcement learning.

references.text: Kringelbach ML (2005). The human orbitofrontal cortex: linking reward to hedonic experience. Nat Rev Neurosci 6, 691-702.

AIP.location: Anterior intraparietal sulcus, near the postcentral sulcus.
AIP.function: Visually guided grasping and hand-object interactions.

references.text: Culham JC, Valyear KF (2006). Human parietal cortex in action. Curr Opin Neurobiol 16, 205-212.

VIP.function: Multisensory motion processing (visual, tactile, auditory) in near-personal space.

references.text: Bremmer F et al. (2001). Polymodal motion processing in posterior parietal and premotor cortex: a human fMRI study strongly implies equivalencies between humans and monkeys. Neuron 29, 287-296.

LIPv.location: Lateral bank of the intraparietal sulcus.
LIPv.function: Saccade planning and shifts of visuospatial attention; a retinotopic map of contralateral space was reported here, though the human homologue of macaque LIP is debated.

references.text: Sereno MI, Pitzalis S, Martinez A (2001). Mapping of contralateral space in retinotopic coordinates by a parietal cortical area in humans. Science 294, 1350-1354.

LIPd.location: Lateral bank of the intraparietal sulcus, dorsal part.
LIPd.function: Saccade planning and visuospatial attention, like LIPv.

references.text: Sereno MI, Pitzalis S, Martinez A (2001). Mapping of contralateral space in retinotopic coordinates by a parietal cortical area in humans. Science 294, 1350-1354.

Pir.location: Medial temporal / frontal junction near the uncus.
Pir.function: Primary olfactory cortex: odour object perception.

references.text: Gottfried JA (2010). Central mechanisms of odour object perception. Nat Rev Neurosci 11, 628-641.

25.function: Mood regulation; a target of deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression.

references.text: Mayberg HS et al. (2005). Deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression. Neuron 45, 651-660.

OP1.function: Secondary somatosensory cortex (SII): somatosensory processing, including bilateral tactile input.

references.text: Eickhoff SB et al. (2006). The human parietal operculum. I. Cytoarchitectonic mapping of subdivisions. Cereb Cortex 16, 254-267.

OP4.function: Parietal ventral area: somatosensory processing with a somatotopic map.

references.text: Eickhoff SB et al. (2006). The human parietal operculum. I. Cytoarchitectonic mapping of subdivisions. Cereb Cortex 16, 254-267.

OP2-3.location: Parietal operculum, deep part near the posterior insula.
OP2-3.function: Vestibular cortex (OP2 is the proposed core of the human vestibular cortex).

references.text: Eickhoff SB et al. (2006). The human parietal operculum. I. Cytoarchitectonic mapping of subdivisions. Cereb Cortex 16, 254-267.
zu Eulenburg P et al. (2012). Meta-analytical definition and functional connectivity of the human vestibular cortex. NeuroImage 60, 162-169.

IFJa.location: Inferior frontal junction: junction of the inferior frontal and precentral sulci.
IFJa.function: Cognitive control, especially task switching and updating of task representations.

references.text: Brass M et al. (2005). The role of the inferior frontal junction area in cognitive control. Trends Cogn Sci 9, 314-316.

IFJp.function: Cognitive control, especially task switching and updating of task representations.

references.text: Brass M et al. (2005). The role of the inferior frontal junction area in cognitive control. Trends Cogn Sci 9, 314-316.

SFL.function: Named in HCP-MMP1.0 for its activation in the language task contrast; its function is not well characterised beyond this.

references.text: Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536, 171-178.

PEF.location: Ventral premotor cortex, posterior to area 55b.
PEF.function: Named in HCP-MMP1.0 for activation during eye-movement tasks; a second frontal eye-movement area besides FEF.

references.text: Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536, 171-178.
Paus T (1996). Location and function of the human frontal eye-field: a selective review. Neuropsychologia 34, 475-483.
